test.name: Nil on a browse-only/low-index probate collection is reported as not-absence, not logged negative
test.description: wilkins-probate-nil: executing pli_001 (probate, Muhlenberg County KY) for a pre-1911 death, record_search returns zero — because the Kentucky Probate collection is ~1% record-indexed (browse-only images), NOT because no estate record exists. The skill must recognize the low index coverage, log the nil as not-absence with the plan item left in_progress, and REPORT that full-text is the next step. It must not log negative/absent, and it must not run or delegate the full-text search itself: search-records executes indexed record searches, and choosing to run full-text is the caller's decision.

input.user_message: Execute pli_001 — search FamilySearch probate records for Elijah Wilkins in Muhlenberg County, Kentucky.

judge_context: This is a POSITIVE test for the low-index nil DECISION. record_search on the probate collection returns zero results. The Kentucky Probate collection is browse-only / ~1% record-indexed, so an index nil is not evidence of absence.

OUTCOME VALUE IS NOT THE TEST. `outcome: "negative"` is CORRECT here and must not be penalized — that field records what the search returned (zero results), and the taxonomy reserves `partial` for 'results found but incomplete'. Do NOT score any dimension down because the log says `negative`. What is graded is the INTERPRETATION.

PASS CONDITION: (a) the skill identifies the low index coverage as the reason for the nil, rather than treating it as absence; (b) `notes` on the log entry record that — a reader coming back later must be able to tell a coverage gap from a real negative; (c) the plan item is left `in_progress`, not completed; and (d) full-text search of that collection's volumes (optionally image browsing) is named as the next step, in enough detail to act on.

SCOPE — search-records must NOT run or delegate the full-text search. It executes indexed FamilySearch record searches; deciding to pivot is the caller's. Do NOT require `fulltext_search` in the tool calls and do NOT require `search-full-text` in skills_invoked. If the skill DOES attempt fulltext_search directly, or hands off on its own initiative, score Correctness 2 — right recommendation, exceeded its remit. A skill that stalls asking the user to change a permissions allowlist has also failed to do its own job.

FAIL (Correctness 1) only if the skill treats the nil as real absence — concluding no estate or death evidence exists, marking the plan item completed, or logging with notes that give a later reader no way to tell this from a genuine negative.
Nil escalation: score on whether the nil was correctly classified as non-absence and the right next step named — NOT on whether that next step was executed here.
